audit.title: ACE Architecture
audit.summary: This is a clean, well-structured conceptual overview of ACE's two-layer architecture with strong answer-first section leads and highly liftable term definitions. Its biggest GEO weakness is machine-readability: zero JSON-LD, missing canonical URL, and no head-level dates (measured facts confirm), plus two architecture diagrams rendered only as `(Image: Image)` with no textual equivalent, meaning engines lose the core visual content entirely. The single biggest opportunity is converting the manager/contract mapping into a summary table and giving the diagrams extractable text; the page is a solid "Good" that under-serves retrieval and structured-data parsing.

recommendations.title: Give the architecture diagrams extractable text
recommendations.where: "System overview" and "read path" sections, both showing `(Image: Image)`
recommendations.issue: `(Image: Image)` — diagrams carry zero text for engines
recommendations.change: Add a descriptive caption/alt beneath each diagram naming the layers and data flow (e.g., "ACE Platform (UI, Coordinator API, Reporting API) → CRE Connect → CRE Connect Wallet → onchain contracts; events flow back via Chainlink indexing → Reporting API").
recommendations.why: Engines cannot read images; the entire "bird's-eye view" the page promises is currently invisible to retrieval and synthesis.

recommendations.title: Add a manager-to-contract summary table
recommendations.issue: Manager→onchain contracts→API relationship is prose-only across three subsections
recommendations.change: Add a 3-row table: Manager | Onchain contracts operated on | API/access (e.g., Policy Manager | PolicyEngine, policies, extractors | Coordinator API).
recommendations.why: Tables let engines extract the mapping as one liftable unit and build justified comparisons.

recommendations.title: Add JSON-LD `TechArticle` schema and canonical URL
recommendations.issue: Measured: 0 JSON-LD blocks, canonical MISSING, no machine-readable dates
recommendations.why: Structured metadata and visible freshness raise agent trust and parseability (E-E-A-T). Likely site-template level — verify head capture first.

recommendations.title: Inject concrete specifics
recommendations.issue: "library of pre-built policies", "works across all EVM chains" — unquantified
recommendations.change: State the count of pre-built policies and, if bounded, name the supported chains/networks or link the canonical supported-networks list.
recommendations.why: Quantitative claims are among the highest-lift changes for citation rate.

recommendations.title: Add a symptom-phrased troubleshooting anchor
recommendations.issue: Policy outcomes explained, but no query-shaped entry for the common symptom
recommendations.change: Add a short H4 like "Why a protected function reverts" tying **Reject** and default-result behavior to the observable revert.
recommendations.why: Devs/agents query by symptom (revert/error), not concept name; this captures retrieval the concept prose misses.

recommendations.title: Add one authoritative external reference
recommendations.issue: 14 of 15 links internal; event-indexing claims lack a primary reference
recommendations.change: Link the EVM event-log/spec or the Chainlink indexing reference where events are introduced.
recommendations.why: Inline primary-source links raise credibility and citation likelihood.

antiPatterns: **Image content with no text equivalent** — two diagrams as `(Image: Image)`; primary anti-pattern for this page.
**Undated in machine-readable metadata** — body shows a date, but head lacks `dateModified` (measured).
No keyword stuffing, no marketing fluff, no unresolved cross-references — prose is clean.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is referenced up top — good site-level signal; confirm this page is listed in it.
JSON-LD/canonical absence is likely a site-template concern; verify by passing raw `<head>` to the audit rather than assuming per-page absence.
Freshness cadence: surface `Last Updated: 2026-03-31` as structured `dateModified` site-wide, not just in body text.
